episodes.title: AI Roll-Ups: Buy a Boring Business, Run It with Agents
summary: Greg Isenberg's X article makes the case for AI roll-ups: buy an established services business and run its back office with AI agents.
His playbook: buy the customers and trust, build a rulebook and review checkpoints, and move margins from 5-10% toward 30-40%.
Guests add balance: even Thrive needed more than off-the-shelf AI, and AI users get less accurate when they stop checking.

episodes.title: Why Software Factories Fail: The Harness Is Not Enough
summary: Dex Horthy's X article, part one of Why Software Factories Fail, argues the lights-off software factory does not work.
Coding models are trained to pass tests, and there is no penalty for eroding codebase maintainability.
Guests add DORA and METR data on delivery stability and developer speed, plus how SWE-bench tasks are graded.

In this episode:

- Why models are rewarded for passing tests, not good design
- What DORA and METR data say about stability and speed

episodes.title: Your Coding Agents Made You a Manager
summary: Addy Osmani's X article Your coding agents made you a manager: the skills for managing agents are the skills for managing a team.

Guests bring the Wharton cognitive surrender study via Gizmodo and METR's trial where developers were 19% slower with AI.
